A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

If you’re energized by the idea of making the impossible happen, come join us as a Senior Mechanical Engineer.

Include a portfolio with your application to show us what you can do.

The Job:

The job is to ship the best desktop 3D printers on the market:

• Prototype new mechanisms, from precision latches to revolutionary pumps and valves to surfaces measured in microns

• Test materials that push the boundaries of what 3D printing can do

• Research 3D printing challenges and rethink every subprocess to push technology forward

• Analyze, validate, and iterate on electro-mechanical systems

• Model everything from brackets to hinges to complex parts in CAD, creating well-specified, accurate drawings

• Partner with Global Sourcing and Manufacturing Teams to bring designs from prototype to mass production 

• Flex your global savvy by working with teams around the world, virtually and in-person. Intermittent travel is expected. 

• Apply your knowledge of manufacturing techniques like injection molding and sheet metal fabrication to the world of 3D printing

At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.

We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.

Join a small, scrappy team driving Form Now, our new print-on-demand service that brings professional 3D printing to customers faster and more affordably than ever. You'll design and build the software powering our Form Now website and production line, solve complex technical problems, and play a key role in launching a new class of 3D printing at scale.

What You’ll Do:

• Develop and implement core software features for the Form Now print-on-demand service.

• Architect and build the next generation of factory software, including our custom Manufacturing Execution System (MES).

• Create robust backend code using Python/Django, and user-facing frontend code with Next.js and React.js.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with factory operators, product managers, and leadership to define and deliver new features and integrations.

• Take full ownership of your projects, from initial scoping and development to testing, implementation, and ongoing support.

• Maintain and improve our existing codebase, ensuring reliability and scalability in a production environment.

In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.

Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

Every business pays bills, and many of them still do it by hand. Someone opens the invoice, types it in, codes it, chases approvals, pays it, matches it and syncs it to the books. It's one of the largest manual workflows left in finance.

We're building the version where software does that work. Bills come in and get read, coded, matched, approved and paid, and a person steps in only when judgment matters. Bill Pay is already one of Ramp's fastest-growing products. The next few years decide who owns AP for the next decade, and we plan for it to be us.

We're looking for a PM who wants to build that.

 - Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week.

About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. 

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. 

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Veeva is the industry cloud for Life Sciences. We are enabling agentic biopharma through applications, agents, data, and consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website.
 
Consulting is changing, and Veeva Business Consulting is not like other firms. Launched in 2019, we’ve grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep industry knowledge and unique insights to accelerate drug development and commercialization for our customers.
 
We are growing aggressively and seeking great people to help Life Sciences work in a more efficient and connected way, shaping the future of the industry with the world’s leading AI applications, agents, and data at their back.
 
The Role
We are hiring recent university graduates to grow the next generation of consultants through our Business Consultant Development Program (BCDP).
 
We believe in pushing high potential people to achieve excellence. Our program is specifically designed to provide a challenging environment to learn quickly and deliver value early. You will collaborate with experienced team members on customer-facing engagements to create high-impact business solutions.
 
In our structured 20 month program, we equip you with the resources to develop the core consulting skills, deep domain expertise, and leadership foundation for long-term career success at Veeva.
 
BCDP spans five core practice areas: Analytics, Commercial, Content, R&D, and Quality. As an Associate Consultant you will align to one of those practices, allowing you to build targeted industry expertise. You will be asked to choose your preferred practice in the application process.
 
You can learn more about our practices and the work we do here.
